correctness.rationale: The classification follows exactly from prime-factor exponents of \(n\) and \(arphi(n)\): \(n=2^a p^b\) is Achilles iff \(a,b\ge2\) and \(\gcd(a,b)=1\); \(arphi(n)=2^{a+t-1}p^{b-1}\prod_j q_j^{c_j}\), so powerfulness and non-perfect-power status give precisely the stated remaining inequalities and gcd. The asymptotic is a two-dimensional lattice-density argument: each prime forbids one or two explicitly distinct residue pairs, finite-prime densities combine by CRT, and the tail is controlled by the convergent sum of reciprocal prime squares. The standalone checker made 13005 direct definition-versus-criterion comparisons and matched all 21 two-prime-support terms in the displayed OEIS prefix through 135000.

value.rationale: The classification component is a useful exact specialization of the known exponent test, while the substantive added value is quantitative: every admissible two-prime support \(\{2,p\}\) receives an explicit positive asymptotic constant, and inadmissible supports are identified exactly. This turns a decision/enumeration framework into a support-wise density law tied to the exponent pattern of \(p-1\), rather than merely recomputing a finite table.
